A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Table-R1 work. Complete text extraction and rendered-page comparison cover the main paper and Appendices A-B, with no material reading gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original GRPO and Table-R1 experiments, including reasoning accuracy, perception scores and ablations in Tables 1 and 3-9.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including Table-R1 benchmark evaluations and component ablations.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A retain identical warm-up, PA-GRPO and HC-GRPO procedures, rewards, objectives and pseudocode.

E1.justification: Both versions use WTQ, HiTab, TabMWP and TabFact as held-in datasets and TAT-QA and InfoTabs as held-out datasets. The evaluated reasoning and perception tasks are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in the corresponding experiments, including SFT, GRPO, Table-LLaVA 7B/13B, other open- and closed-source LVLMs, and the ablation comparators in Tables 5-9.

E3.justification: Sections 5.2-5.3 retain the same sampling, image and output filtering, accuracy and TEDS metrics, model sizes, training budgets and testing procedures. Ablation configurations also remain identical.

E4.justification: Stage ablations, generation-count and hint-split sensitivity, PA-GRPO/SFT comparisons, HC-GRPO comparisons and reward curves are unchanged. Appendix B.4 retains the same five failure categories and their frequency ordering.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version adds repeated-run counts, evaluation seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical results, plotted findings and qualitative outcomes are identical. For example, Table 3 reports Qwen2-VL-7B-Table-R1 averages of 68.63% held-in and 55.43% held-out in both versions.

T1.justification: Section 3 retains the same Bernoulli-reward variance argument. The problem formulation and Equations 1-8 are identical, with no added or revised mathematical reasoning or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain identical claims about initialization sensitivity, the three-stage framework, improvements over SFT/GRPO and performance comparable to GPT-4o on held-in datasets.

C2.justification: Interpretations of initialization sensitivity and component effectiveness are unchanged. Both retain the same limitations concerning definitive-answer tasks, English benchmarks with clear images, and binary HC-GRPO rewards, alongside identical appendix failure explanations.

D1.justification: Hardware, optimization settings, preprocessing details and Math-Verify access information are identical. Appendices A-B retain the same pseudocode and prompt templates, with no changes to code or data access information.

R1.justification: The existing DAPO citation, Yu et al. (2025), retains the same role in Section 3. Its bibliography entry receives authorship, title and publication-metadata revisions, without changing cited-work coverage or research positioning.

P1.justification: The DAPO entry changes from Hang Yu et al., 'Data-aware policy optimization for open-source llm alignment,' to Qiying Yu et al., 'An open-source llm reinforcement learning system at scale,' with NeurIPS 2025 publication details. The arXiv version/date stamp also changes; body and appendix wording and structure remain identical.

P2.justification: The expanded DAPO entry changes reference spacing and flows across columns on page 12. Figures 1-6, Tables 1-10 and Algorithm 1 retain identical content, formatting and placement.

improvement.justification: v3 updates one bibliography entry and its associated layout, while preserving all methods, evidence, interpretations, limitations and appendix material. This localized bibliographic revision does not meaningfully change the paper's overall scientific support, reproducibility or clarity.
